title: Stateless vs Stateful Widgets in Flutter

scenes.say: Which widget type should you use, stateless or stateful, and why does it matter in Flutter?

scenes.label: Stateless
scenes.sub: Immutable. No internal state. UI updates only if input changes.
scenes.say: Stateless widgets are immutable. They don't store any state and only update when their input data changes.

scenes.label: Stateful
scenes.sub: Holds mutable state. Rebuilds when state changes.
scenes.say: Stateful widgets hold mutable state. If that state changes, the widget rebuilds to show the new data.
Use stateless widgets for static screens. Choose stateful when your UI needs to react to user input or data changes.
Here's what the code looks like for each type. Stateless widgets have no state, while stateful widgets can update their UI when their state changes.

scenes.question: When does a StatelessWidget rebuild?
scenes.right: Whenever its input parameters change, even from external data.
scenes.say: Careful—stateless widgets can rebuild if their input changes, not just when the parent changes.
